title: Air India Crash Probe Enters Final Stages as Cockpit Voice Recorder Transcript Is Prepared
excerpt: India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau has moved into the analysis phase of its inquiry into the Boeing 787 crash that killed 260 people, with a final report expected within six weeks.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • The AAIB's investigation into the Air India crash is in its final analysis phase.
  • A cockpit voice recorder transcript and psychological autopsy have been prepared.
  • A lawsuit by the captain's father revealed implications of pilot error in the crash.
  • Media narratives have hindered witness cooperation in the investigation.
  • The final report is expected within six weeks, pending external factors.
Investigation Progress Overview
›Investigation moved to analysis phase.
›Cockpit voice recorder transcript prepared.
›Psychological autopsy conducted.
›Final report expected in six weeks.
AAIB court filing
  • India's AAIB has prepared a cockpit voice recorder transcript and conducted a psychological autopsy as part of its investigation into the June 2025 Air India crash
  • The probe is now in the analysis phase, with findings expected within approximately six weeks pending external dependencies
  • A lawsuit filed by the captain's father prompted the disclosure after investigators allegedly implied his son deliberately cut fuel to the engines
  • Media speculation and blame narratives have caused some witnesses to become uncooperative, the AAIB told the court

Investigation Reaches Analysis Phase

India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau has moved into the final stages of its probe into the Air India Boeing 787 crash that killed 260 people shortly after takeoff from Ahmedabad in June 2025, according to a court filing reviewed by Reuters.

The bureau disclosed that it has prepared a cockpit voice recorder transcript and conducted a psychological autopsy, though the filing did not identify whose autopsy was conducted or reveal any conclusions. An analysis of data retrieved in late May from an engine monitoring unit is still pending, and an assessment of certain organisational factors remains in progress.

Investigators have interviewed Air India 787 pilots, crew members who had previously flown with the pilots of the crashed aircraft, technical personnel involved in preparing the jet, air traffic controllers, weather officials, and human-factors specialists, the AAIB said.

"The other pilot responded that he had not done so."

Father's Lawsuit Forces Disclosure

The new details emerged from a court filing tied to a lawsuit by Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, the father of Captain Sumeet Sabharwal, who commanded the doomed flight. The elder Sabharwal said AAIB officials who visited his home during the early stages of the investigation implied his son had deliberately cut fuel to the aircraft's engines after takeoff.

"The very nature of the investigation and the peculiar nature of the legal regime mean that it takes time to reach the root cause."

— Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, in its court filing

The AAIB told the court that media speculation and narratives attributing blame to the pilots had caused some witnesses to become "restrictive and non-responsive," complicating the investigation. The bureau emphasised that the purpose of an aircraft accident investigation is solely to improve aviation safety and prevent future accidents, not to apportion blame or determine civil or criminal liability.

Key Events Leading to the Crash
June 12, 2025
Flight 171 took off from Ahmedabad at 08:08:39 GMT.
June 12, 2025
Fuel cutoff switches transitioned to CUTOFF position.
June 12, 2025
Cockpit recording revealed pilot confusion over fuel cutoff.
July 2025
Preliminary investigation report released.
Preliminary investigation report

What the Preliminary Report Revealed

According to the preliminary investigation report released in July 2025, the Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner operating as Flight 171 from Ahmedabad to London lifted off at 08:08:39 GMT on June 12, 2025. Three seconds later, at maximum airspeed of 180 knots, the Engine 1 and Engine 2 fuel cutoff switches transitioned from RUN to CUTOFF position within one second of each other.

In the cockpit voice recording, one pilot was heard asking the other why he had cut off the fuel. The other pilot responded that he had not done so. CCTV footage showed the Ram Air Turbine deploying during the initial climb immediately after liftoff as the aircraft lost altitude before crossing the airport perimeter wall.

What Comes Next

The AAIB said it expected the remaining investigation activities to be completed within approximately six weeks, subject to pending "external dependencies." That timeline would place a draft final report around late August or September 2026 — more than a year after the crash.

In a separate development, the bureau has opposed a request by petitioners for access to cockpit voice recorder recordings, citing Rule 17(5) of the Aircraft (Investigation of Accidents and Incidents) Rules, 2025, which imposes an absolute prohibition on public disclosure of cockpit voice recordings. The case has reached India's Supreme Court, where the captain's father has asked for an independent investigation considering causes beyond pilot action.

The crash of Flight 171 remains the deadliest aviation disaster in India's history and one of the worst involving a Boeing 787 Dreamliner worldwide. The investigation has drawn intense scrutiny from aviation safety experts, the families of victims, and Boeing, the aircraft manufacturer.
